question: From 2013 to 2025, how did motorist deaths compare with cyclist deaths in NYC each year?

options.metric: Annual deaths among motorists and cyclists
options.reason: Side-by-side annual counts show both the scale and year-to-year pattern for each group.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year; motorist deaths ranged from 72 to 139 annually, while cyclist deaths ranged from 10 to 31.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the question by showing each group’s annual death count side by side, and the chart shows a higher motorist count in all 13 years. Absolute counts are a direct comparison of deaths recorded in these crash data. It leaves differences in population or travel exposure unaddressed.

options.metric: Motorist deaths minus cyclist deaths per year
options.chart_type: Bar chart of annual count differences
options.reason: The annual difference makes the size and direction of the gap easy to compare across years.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths every year, with the gap ranging from 51 deaths in 2019 to 115 in 2021.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how far apart the annual death counts were, and every bar is positive, indicating more motorist than cyclist deaths in each year. The count difference is a defensible summary of the comparison, especially for seeing when the gap widened or narrowed. It leaves the separate annual totals and any exposure-adjusted risk comparison less explicit.

answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year from 2013 to 2025; motorist deaths ranged from 72 to 139 annually, compared with 10 to 31 cyclist deaths. The annual gap was also positive every year, ranging from 51 deaths in 2019 to 115 in 2021.
